scope: two-seed development, teacher-forced mean reference-completion CE
conclusion: Retaining fitting-row magnitudes does not improve accurate effect-size prediction in this fixed dictionary comparison. Both geometries underestimate the mean effect and fail the prespecified accuracy requirements at the meaningful larger rate.
findings: At rate 0.003, normalized/magnitude nRMSE is 0.728/0.751 in seed42 and 0.757/0.761 in seed43; both exceed the frozen 0.5 limit.
At rate 0.003, normalized/magnitude MAE is 0.01742/0.01803 in seed42 and 0.01976/0.01982 nats/token in seed43; all exceed 0.01.
Magnitude-fit has greater paired MSE than normalized-fit in seed42 at both rates; the prespecified simultaneous intervals exclude zero. Seed43 intervals include zero at both rates.
Normalized predictions capture about 28%/24% of the mean observed CE decrease in seeds42/43 at rate 0.003; magnitude-fit about 25%/24%.
Full-gradient linearization has nRMSE 0.0211/0.0217 at 0.0003 and 0.2634/0.2319 at 0.003. Its worst larger-rate errors remain 0.1471/0.1368 nats/token.
Both dictionary arms improve on zero prediction but do not clear the required accuracy. At the smaller rate actual RMS is 0.00317/0.00343, below the fixed 0.01 meaningful-effect floor.
No negative predicted CE values occur in the retained evaluation pairs.
interpretation: The large dictionary error relative to the full-gradient reference is consistent with representation loss; restoring a scalar norm cannot restore missing directional components. This comparison does not isolate all mechanisms or validate SVD, interpretation, or generated behavior.
decision: Complete the frozen SVD comparison and use its full evidence to decide at most one focused follow-up. Do not retune dictionary penalties or normalization on these outcomes.
limits: Two reused adapters and one synthetic-reference source; development only.
Source and lexical deduplication is not full semantic independence.
Direction agreement is evaluated only on eligible pairs with substantial predicted and actual changes; it is not an overall accuracy claim.
